subject.title: Feature: Inter-session progress streaming for sessions_send (ACP/long-running session support)

question: Should OpenClaw expose peer run progress through a new `sessions_subscribe`/`agent.events` contract, a `sessions_send` progress option, or a broader structured process-event API?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent API shape controls authorization, redaction, buffering, replay, retention, and channel delivery across stable gateway/session surfaces.

options.title: Approve additive run-event observation
options.body: Define a permission-checked, redacted, bounded run-event read API and expose it through a small caller-facing session tool after security review.

options.title: Fold into structured process events
options.body: Treat this as a consumer of #52826 and keep #54895 open only as a sessions_send use case until the broader process-event contract lands.

options.title: Defer peer streaming
options.body: Keep only current wait/history/final-announce behavior and close this feature if maintainers do not want cross-session progress observation in core.

recommendation.title: Approve additive run-event observation
recommendation.body: Define a permission-checked, redacted, bounded run-event read API and expose it through a small caller-facing session tool after security review.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to steipete across sessions_send, A2A flow, agent events, and gateway registration, making him the best available owner for the API-direction choice.
